_policy: Facts and quotes MUST include source_name and source_url pointing to a reliable source. Items without a verifiable source must use type 'encouragement'. Never add invented quotes, records or 'first person to' claims.

items.message: The World Health Organization's global recommendation for adults is at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity per week.
items.source_name: World Health Organization — Physical activity fact sheet

items.message: NHS guidelines for adults aged 19 to 64 suggest at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity a week, and list brisk walking as one example.
items.source_name: NHS — Physical activity guidelines for adults aged 19 to 64

items.message: The 42.195 km marathon distance was standardised in 1921, based on the course length used at the 1908 London Olympics.
A journey of a thousand miles starts with a single step.
items.attribution: Laozi, Tao Te Ching, ch. 64 (common English rendering)

items.message: Every square you fill is proof you showed up. Small days count.
Rest is part of the plan. Resume when you're ready — your record is still yours.
Steady beats intense. A target you can repeat is a target that works.
A walk today is a walk banked. Find a pace where you could still hold a conversation.
Distance is built patiently. Easy days make the hard ones possible.
WinterArc isn't medical or coaching advice. Choose targets that suit your current ability, build gradually, and stop if something hurts.
